action: Apply SonicWall's SonicOS updates for Gen7 and Gen8 firewalls after testing, starting with devices using SAML for SSLVPN, and keep firewall management interfaces off the internet.
exec: A firewall VPN flaw that can sidestep MFA is on the exploited list; risk is rated high for government and business of every size.
plain: SonicWall firewalls have security flaws, one of which can let someone get past the extra sign-in check on the VPN. The US cyber agency already lists that flaw as being used by attackers.

key_findings: SonicOS Gen7 hardware and NSv at 7.3.3-7015 and earlier, and Gen8 at 8.2.2-8015 and earlier, are affected.
Two management-interface flaws let remote unauthenticated attackers perform unauthorised operations under specific conditions; internet-exposed interfaces are at higher risk.
CVE-2026-19868 lets a user holding valid credentials for another method bypass SAML, and possibly SAML-enforced MFA, on SSLVPN.
SonicWall investigated a report of possible exploitation of CVE-2026-19868, and CISA added it to the KEV catalog on November 6.
Three further flaws are pre-authentication overflows causing denial of service; risk is rated High for all government and business sizes.
recommendations: Apply SonicWall's updates promptly after appropriate testing.
Run a risk-based remediation process with reviews at least monthly.
Apply least privilege and disable or secure default accounts.
Segment the network and administer devices from dedicated resources without internet access.

summary: MS-ISAC advisory 2026-126 covers seven flaws in SonicWall SonicOS on Gen7 firewalls up to 7.3.3-7015 and Gen8 up to 8.2.2-8015. Two management-interface bugs let remote unauthenticated attackers perform unauthorised operations under certain conditions. CVE-2026-19868 lets a user with other valid credentials skip SAML, and possibly MFA, on SSLVPN; SonicWall investigated a report of exploitation and CISA listed it as exploited on November 6.
title: MS-ISAC: SonicWall SonicOS flaws allow authentication bypass; one SSLVPN bug is already on CISA's KEV list

validation.note: Reviewed against the original MS-ISAC document.
